pages.title: Quick start: your first class website
pages.question: How do I get from nothing to a class website, without any account?
steps: What you need: a Mac with Apple silicon and macOS 15; no account for the first site; an assistant is optional (link github-education)
Download Plantoir from plantoir.app and drag it into Applications
Open it and choose an empty folder as your working folder (Choose Folder…, then Set Up This Folder)
Wait while Plantoir gets this Mac ready (first time only, a few minutes)
File ▸ New Course…: type the course code and keep the ready-made pages if offered
In the same sheet's Deploying part, set Deploy to: A folder on this Mac, press Choose… and pick an empty folder (for example Class Sites in Documents); make the course
Select Section 1 in the sidebar and press Preview; read the site in the window, or Open in Browser
Press Deploy and answer the checklist; the site is copied into section1 inside your folder
Press Open in Browser. The site opens in your browser, served from the folder (#850)

pages.title: Put your site online with Cloudflare Pages
pages.question: When I am ready for students to open the site, how do I put it online?
steps: Make a free Cloudflare account
In Cloudflare, create an API token with one permission: Account, Cloudflare Pages, Edit; copy your Account ID
Plantoir ▸ Settings ▸ Deploying: paste the Cloudflare Account ID (once, for every course)
Course Settings ▸ Deploying: set Deploy to: Cloudflare Pages (keep the folder as Also deploy to, if you like); Save
Select the section and Deploy; paste the API token when asked (first deploy only)
The result says Your website is live with the address; give that address to your class

pages.title: Shared pages and section pages
pages.question: Which pages does every section get, and which belong to one section?
steps: Every folder at the top of the course is shared: each section's site includes it
A section's own folder (section1, section2) holds its front page, All Classes, Key Links, Private Notes and Scratch Page
A shared page can still be published for one section and not another: its settings carry one line per section
A page in a section's folder with the same name and place as a shared one replaces the shared one on that section's site
In the example course, open Key Links in section1 and section2: each section keeps its own

pages.title: Class pages: Unit 1, Day 1

The front page shows Most Recent Class: the newest class students can see
A page named another way (Field Trip, Exam Review) is kept as it is and never renumbered
